a double rf system subjected to sinusoidal modulation of the rf phase exhibits a tree of bifurtion branches which can be understood as a sequence of parametric resonance bifurcations.

the stability and dynamics of the motion of a particle in a double rf system.
the stability of the fixed points of the Poincare sections of the synchrotron motion.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the phase modulation of a double rf system in a synchrotron leads to parametric resonances.
the phase modulation of a double rf system can be used to generate a rich spectrum of stable and unstable fixed points which are useful to study the stability of the system.
the parametric resonances in double rf systems can be understood as bifurcations of fixed points on Poincare surfaces.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the bifurcation branches of stable and unstable fixed points in the Poincare surface of section are generated by parametric resonance.
the phase modulation of a synchrotron with a single rf system is equivalent to that of a synchrotro with two rf systems.
parametric resonances in the double rf system can be described by the theory of parametric resonance in a single degree of freedom.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the parametric resonance is the key mechanism for the generation of the bifurcation branches.
parametric resonances are generated in a double rf system by phase modulation, and the stability of these resonance islands is controlled by the amplitude of the modulation.
the stability of the fixed points of a resonance island can be determined by the phase modulation of the rf system.
